How it is checked: Not measured yet: needs a load test against the deployed backend.
What the SRS says: The feed and listing-detail endpoints should respond within 1.5 s (95th percentile) over campus Wi-Fi under pilot load.

How it is checked: Not measured yet: needs a load test against the deployed backend.
What the SRS says: The system should support at least 100 concurrent users and semester-start spikes of several hundred new listings per day without degradation.

How it is checked: Inspection: indexes on listings (status, category) and (owner_id) in migration 000; the test database is built from the same migrations.
What the SRS says: Feed queries shall use indexes on (status, category) and owner.

How it is checked: The 8 MB limit is tested (a larger upload gets 413). Compressing photos in the app before upload is not built.
What the SRS says: Images shall be limited to 8 MB on upload, and the app should compress photos before uploading to save mobile data.

How it is checked: Manual: two phones in one chat (MT-CHT-10).
What the SRS says: A sent chat message should appear for the other participant within 5 s (Supabase Realtime, with a slow fallback poll).
Every non-public endpoint shall validate the bearer token before running any business logic and return 401 if it is missing, invalid or expired.
Authorisation (admin role, listing ownership, chat participation, offer recipient) shall be enforced on the server; client-side checks are for display only.

How it is checked: Also by inspection: .env files are git-ignored and the app only has the public key.
What the SRS says: The service-role key shall exist only in the backend environment; secrets shall be kept in git-ignored .env files.

How it is checked: Admin ID-card queue returns signed links valid for 600 s.
What the SRS says: ID card images shall be stored in a private bucket and exposed only to admins through signed URLs that expire in 10 minutes.
Row-Level Security shall be enabled on all tables before any wider release, so the public (anon) key cannot read or write tables directly.

All input shall be validated at the API boundary (types, lengths, enums, file type and size). Photos are checked by their contents (JPEG, PNG, WebP or HEIC only), cut off at 8 MB while uploading, and stored under names the server chooses; listings and offers may only use photos the student uploaded.
QR codes shall be random, single-use, bound to one transaction and expire after 10 minutes.

How it is checked: Deployment only (HTTPS is provided by the host); nothing is deployed yet.
What the SRS says: All traffic in deployment shall use HTTPS.
Each signed-in session shall be rate limited per endpoint (120 requests and 30 writes a minute, 20 new listings an hour, 40 photo uploads per 10 minutes); a request over the limit receives 429.

How it is checked: Header test; the dependency audit is a step in CI (ci.yml).
What the SRS says: Responses shall carry standard security headers, browser access shall be limited to configured origins in deployment, and CI shall fail on a high or critical vulnerability in a production dependency.

How it is checked: Inspection: the users table holds only email, name, roll number, hostel and the ID-card path.
What the SRS says: The system shall collect only the identity data needed: email, name, roll number and ID-card image.

How it is checked: Guest feed and detail have no meeting location.
What the SRS says: A guest shall never receive a listing's meeting location.
A user's email and roll number shall not be shown to other students.
Condition photographs shall be stored privately (encrypted at rest by the storage provider) and shown only to the two parties and admins, through links that expire.

How it is checked: One account per roll number, also refused by the database.
What the SRS says: Each roll number shall belong to at most one account.

How it is checked: Needs monitoring of the deployed system during the pilot.
What the SRS says: Login, listing and payment shall be available at least 99\% of the time during peak hours of the pilot.

How it is checked: Escrow and deal status are checked together in the payment tests; not every multi-step write runs as one database transaction yet.
What the SRS says: Related writes shall be atomic: a listing and its moderation entry are created together or not at all; escrow and transaction status shall never disagree.

How it is checked: Exactly one accepted offer per thread.
What the SRS says: Accepting an offer shall leave a thread with exactly one accepted offer.

How it is checked: No test case yet. To check: turn Wi-Fi off in the app and retry an action; expect an error with a retry, not a crash.
What the SRS says: The app shall show clear, retryable errors when the network fails, rather than crashing.

How it is checked: Needs a timed usability test with new students during the pilot.
What the SRS says: A new student should be able to sign up and post a first listing in under 5 minutes without help.

How it is checked: Status wording is checked in MT-PAY-6; the clarity rating needs a pilot survey.
What the SRS says: Transaction status shall always be visible and in plain language; target average clarity rating $$ 4 out of 5.

How it is checked: No test case yet. To check: run the manual cases on a small Android phone.
What the SRS says: Text shall be legible and touch targets adequately sized on small Android screens.

How it is checked: One Expo codebase; run the manual cases on one Android phone and one iPhone.
What the SRS says: The app shall run on both Android and iOS from one codebase.

How it is checked: Not measured yet: needs a budget Android phone (2–3 GB RAM).
What the SRS says: The app should run acceptably on budget Android devices (2–3 GB RAM).

How it is checked: The automated tests run two backend processes side by side on one database; no session state is kept in the backend.
What the SRS says: The backend shall be stateless so it can be deployed on any Node.js cloud host or container platform.

How it is checked: CI type-checks both projects in strict mode on every push.
What the SRS says: Code shall be written in TypeScript (strict mode) and organised by feature module in both app and backend.

How it is checked: Inspection: .github/workflows/ci.yml runs on every push and pull request.
What the SRS says: Each push shall trigger CI that type-checks, lints and unit-tests the mobile app and the backend, runs the end-to-end tests, builds the backend and audits dependencies; failing builds shall not be merged.

How it is checked: The test database is built by running supabase/migrations 000–011 in order.
What the SRS says: Schema changes shall be made through numbered migration files in supabase/migrations.

How it is checked: Inspection: every controller route appears in docs/api-contract.md.
What the SRS says: Every API endpoint shall be documented in docs/api-contract.md.

How it is checked: This document: every functional requirement has an automated or a manual test case.
What the SRS says: Unit and end-to-end tests shall cover every functional requirement that software can check; the rest shall have manual test cases.

How it is checked: Pages of 20, never more than 50; feed queries use the indexes of NFR-PRF-3.
What the SRS says: Listing and search queries should support pagination and indexing so they keep within NFR-PRF-1 as listings grow.

How it is checked: CI is in place; deployment to a staging host is not done yet.
What the SRS says: The system should be deployable with a managed database, a platform-hosted backend and a CI/CD pipeline to staging. (CI is in place; deployment is not yet.)
